locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code encrypts telemetry at rest? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: sealReading() derives the GCM nonce deterministically from keyId and deviceId, so every reading from the same device under the same key reuses one IV. AES-GCM nonce reuse leaks the XOR of plaintexts (exposing GPS positions across readings) and lets an attacker recover the GHASH key and forge authentication tags. The IV must be random (randomBytes(12)) or a never-repeating counter per key.

choiceQuestions.prompt: An attacker with database write access copies a sealed blob from device A's row into a row belonging to device B. What happens when recent() is called for device B?
choices: The reading is returned as if device B had sent it
openReading() throws because the deviceId is bound as additional authenticated data
The row is skipped silently and the remaining readings are returned
The reading is decrypted but its gps field is dropped
choiceQuestions.explanation: Both seal and open call setAAD with the deviceId, so authenticating under device B's id fails in decipher.final() and the error propagates out of the map, rejecting the whole call. Nothing catches the error, so rows are not skipped, and no partial decryption occurs.

choiceQuestions.prompt: After activeKeyId is rotated to a new key, what is required for old rows to remain readable through recent()?
choices: Nothing; recent() only works on rows already rewrapped
Only the new key, because GCM can decrypt with any key from the same ring
The old IVs must be regenerated with the new key id
The old key must stay in ring.keys until rewrapOlderThan() has migrated those rows
choiceQuestions.explanation: openReading() looks up sealed.keyId in ring.keys, so any row still sealed with the old key needs that key present. rewrapOlderThan() decrypts with the old key and reseals with the active one. Decryption needs the exact key, and IVs are stored per row.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Which reading fields are protected by encryption at rest in the telemetry table?
choices: All fields including device_id and recorded_at
Only gps, because the other fields are numeric
gps, batteryPct and sensors; device_id and recorded_at stay in plaintext columns
None; the sealed column stores base64 that anyone can decode
choiceQuestions.explanation: append() seals an object with gps, batteryPct and sensors, while device_id and recorded_at are inserted as plaintext columns needed for indexing and querying. Base64 is just the encoding of the ciphertext, not the plaintext.
